rationale: Evidence: iteration 7 (kd 0.20, otherwise identical to iteration 6) scored 53.35, well below iteration 6 (85.60). Oval progress fell from 0.3425 to 0.115, the same stalled value seen at kd 0.05, 0.15 and 0.20 in earlier races. Oval steering_oscillation did drop to 0.075, below the 0.15 guide, but the damping cut removed the oval gain. The Evaluator's kd 0.20 bet is therefore not supported by the race. Its condition (b) applies: oval progress fell well below 0.3425, so kd returns to 0.30. Iteration 1 showed kd below 0.30 also lost s-bend and slalom progress (0.04 and 0.035 at kd 0.05 and 0.15, versus 0.157 and 0.110 at kd 0.30). Changes: none from the best raced design (iteration 6). kd 0.30, base_speed 1.0, kp 4.0, ki 0.05, search_left, five sensors at x = -0.05 to 0.05 m, y 0.04 m, sensor_size 0.016, and the weights are all as in iteration 6. Expected result: about 85.6 again, with oval progress near 0.34 and s-bend and slalom at one line-loss event each. This is a safe reproduction of the best design, not an improvement. Hypotheses for the next race: (1) oval max_error stays just above 0.06 (0.062), which limits oval progress; (2) oval steering_oscillation stays near 0.19, which is above the guide but apparently needed for progress; (3) s-bend and slalom line losses persist under every recovery direction, so they need a sensor-layout change, not a controller change. Measurements requested: oval progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation, plus s-bend and slalom line_loss_events and progress.
